hypothesis: In published embryo-level counts, Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to 0.1 mg/mL nicotine (stages 10-35) show major brain morphology defects at stage 45 at a much higher rate (about 55%) than untreated controls (about 6%).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: from published counts (affected / scored tadpoles) for nicotine-exposed and control embryos under the claim's protocol, (a) the incidence of major brain defects is >= 40% with nicotine and <= 15% in controls, and (b) the difference is significant by a two-sided Fisher exact test at p < 0.001. If only percentages and group sizes are published, counts are reconstructed as round(percentage x n) and this is stated.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: nicotine incidence minus control incidence < 10 percentage points, or Fisher p >= 0.05. Outcomes in between (significant but outside the magnitude bands in (a)) are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If no counts or group sizes for both groups can be obtained from a public source, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).
planned_datasets: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M (2018) HCN2 rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns. Nat Commun 9:998, doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5: full text (Europe PMC), figure legends and any Source Data / supplementary files
Other published embryo-level counts of Xenopus brain defects after embryonic nicotine exposure, if found in Europe PMC full text (secondary, independent where from other studies)
interpretation: 'Major brain morphology defects' follows the paper's scoring (absent nostrils, forebrain or midbrain, or misformed hindbrain at stage 45). The test checks that the published counts support the stated incidence contrast; with only the source paper's data available it is an audit of the reported numbers, not an independent replication, and is labelled as such. Mortality differences, clutch structure and blinding cannot be assessed from aggregate counts. The claim's mechanistic context (nicotine acting through disruption of the brain bioelectric prepattern) is not tested.

test_contract.expected_observation: Published counts give >= 40% major brain defects with 0.1 mg/mL nicotine and <= 15% in controls, Fisher p < 0.001.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A difference of less than 10 percentage points between nicotine and controls, or Fisher p >= 0.05.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public embryo-level or group-level counts (scored n and affected n, or percentage and n) of stage-45 Xenopus brain morphology after nicotine exposure in the claim's dose and window; the source paper's own data are admissible but not independent; other labs' counts are preferred where they exist.
test_contract.inference_method: Incidence per group from counts; two-sided Fisher exact test of nicotine vs control; apply the magnitude bands and p thresholds.
